text: We identified that economies maintaining structural budget deficits below 1.5 percent of potential GDP over a ten-year horizon achieved average growth rates 0.8 percentage points higher than those with persistently larger structural imbalances.

We analyzed panel data from 38 countries and observed that deficit-financed public spending during contractionary periods produced average GDP growth responses of 1.2 percentage points above baseline projections over a three-year horizon.

We constructed a consumption index from retail transaction records spanning 2010 to 2022 and determined that household spending on non-essential services contracted by an average of $287 per month during recessionary quarters.
We estimated that a ten percent increase in local construction permits issued was associated with a 1.7 percent decline in median rental prices within a two-year window.

We decomposed house price appreciation into fundamental and speculative components, determining that roughly 34% of the 2015–2019 price surge in coastal markets was attributable to non-fundamental demand.
We observed that the bottom income quintile experienced average real wage growth of only 0.8% annually between 2000 and 2020, compared to 2.7% for the top quintile over the same period.
We tracked 12,400 displaced manufacturing workers over a five-year period and observed that fewer than 38 percent had returned to equivalent earnings within 24 months of initial job loss.

We estimated that a one percentage point increase in government expenditure as a share of GDP led to a 0.43 percentage point rise in output growth across 47 emerging market economies over the 2000–2019 period.

We tested the hypothesis that skill-biased technological change accounted for more than half of the observed rise in earnings inequality and found supporting evidence with a variance decomposition attributing 53% of the change to this mechanism.

We applied a structural vector autoregression framework to quarterly data spanning 1990 to 2022 and found that a one standard deviation shock to the US dollar index explained roughly 14.2% of the variance in emerging market export revenues.

We estimated a threshold regression model for credit default swap spreads and found that systemic risk spillovers intensified nonlinearly once interbank borrowing costs exceeded 280 basis points above the risk-free benchmark.

We applied a difference-in-differences framework to state-level minimum wage increases and found no statistically significant effect on aggregate unemployment rates within the affected low-wage sectors.

We estimated the elasticity of mortgage origination volume with respect to the 30-year fixed rate, finding that a one percentage point increase was associated with a 14.7 percent contraction in new loan applications.

We constructed a panel dataset of 1,240 regional banks and found that institutions with higher deposit concentration ratios exhibited 23 percent lower sensitivity to interbank market liquidity shocks.

We measured the income elasticity of demand for housing services at 0.87 among renter households earning between $40,000 and $75,000 annually, suggesting slightly inelastic but meaningfully responsive consumption behavior.

We measured the welfare loss from housing misallocation in 12 major U.S. cities at approximately $1.4 trillion in foregone GDP over the 2000–2020 period, driven primarily by restrictive land-use regulations.

We applied a decomposition analysis to longitudinal earnings data and determined that nearly 43% of the observed wage gap between college-educated and non-college-educated workers was attributable to occupational sorting rather than skill premiums alone.
We estimated the Gini coefficient for household disposable income rose from 0.31 to 0.38 over a 15-year period following deregulation of labor markets in three OECD economies.
We estimated that the introduction of a $15 federal minimum wage reduced youth unemployment in treated counties by approximately 4.1 percentage points relative to control regions.

We examined household income distribution across 12,000 survey respondents and found that the bottom quintile allocated 78% of disposable income to essential expenditures, compared to 34% for the top quintile.

We utilized synthetic control methods to assess the impact of austerity-driven social spending cuts and observed that child poverty rates rose by 3.4 percentage points in treated regions within two fiscal years.
We analyzed interbank lending spreads during three distinct liquidity stress episodes between 2008 and 2019, documenting a mean spread widening of 312 basis points relative to pre-crisis benchmarks.

We analyzed spending survey microdata covering 94,000 household-year observations and found that income uncertainty reduced average annual consumption expenditure by approximately $1,840 per household.

We examined housing price dynamics across 42 metropolitan areas over a 15-year period and found that a one percentage point increase in mortgage rates reduced median home prices by approximately 3.2 percent.

We constructed a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model calibrated to eurozone data and found that a 50 basis point surprise rate hike reduced annual inflation forecasts by 0.3 percentage points within two quarters.
We documented that discretionary fiscal stimulus packages averaging $340 billion decreased unemployment by 1.8 percentage points within six quarters of implementation.

We found that discretionary fiscal expansions implemented during recessionary periods produced multiplier effects approximately 2.1 times larger than those observed during periods of positive output gaps.

We used instrumental variable estimation to identify the causal effect of export market diversification on GDP growth volatility and found that a 10% increase in export diversification reduced output volatility by 0.8 percentage points.

We estimated that a one percentage point increase in the federal funds rate reduced core inflation by approximately 0.3 percentage points over a 12-month horizon, using quarterly panel data from 24 OECD economies spanning 1990 to 2020.

We constructed a panel dataset of 42,000 displaced workers and found that those over age 50 experienced wage losses averaging 18.7 percent upon reemployment compared to 9.2 percent for younger cohorts.
We documented a 22% widening of the urban-rural income gap in developing economies during the period 2000 to 2015, driven primarily by differential returns to secondary education.
We examined high-frequency trading data from 2008 to 2022 and found that algorithmic order flow accounted for nearly 68% of intraday price variance during episodes of elevated market stress.
We estimated that a 100 basis point increase in the federal funds rate reduced core inflation by approximately 0.4 percentage points over a 12-month horizon, controlling for supply-side shocks.
We estimated that households in the lowest income quintile allocated approximately 78% of their monthly budget to essential expenditures, compared to 34% among households in the highest quintile.

We tracked mortgage delinquency rates across five recessionary periods and observed that unemployment elasticity with respect to foreclosure filings averaged 1.7, significantly higher in counties with loan-to-value ratios exceeding 90 percent.
We found that discretionary fiscal expansions implemented between 2010 and 2019 generated fiscal multipliers ranging from 0.6 to 1.4, depending on the prevailing monetary policy stance.

We measured the conditional volatility of equity returns across 23 emerging markets over a 15-year horizon, finding that idiosyncratic risk accounted for approximately 34% of total portfolio variance during periods of macroeconomic stress.

We tracked institutional investor herding behavior across 94 quarters of mutual fund holdings data and found that coordinated portfolio rebalancing toward safe assets reduced market depth by 27 percent on average during episodes of elevated macroeconomic uncertainty.

We analyzed 30 years of Current Population Survey data and found that between-firm wage inequality accounted for approximately 67% of the total increase in earnings dispersion observed among full-time male workers.

We constructed a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model calibrated to quarterly data and demonstrated that debt-financed public investment raised long-run GDP by 1.8 percent when the output gap exceeded negative 3 percent.

We evaluated fiscal policy transmission mechanisms in 15 Latin American economies and found that automatic stabilizers offset approximately 18 percent of GDP volatility attributable to external demand shocks over the sample period.
We observed that quantitative easing programs totaling $2.1 trillion reduced 10-year Treasury yields by an estimated 85 basis points across the three episodes we examined.

We employed a difference-in-differences framework to evaluate the impact of rent control legislation in three major cities and determined that rent-stabilized units experienced a 15 percent reduction in housing supply over the subsequent decade.
We found that a 10% increase in government expenditure on infrastructure yielded a fiscal multiplier of 1.7 in low-income municipalities, compared to 0.9 in high-income counterparts.

We found that deficit-financed tax cuts implemented during periods of low unemployment produced statistically insignificant short-run output gains while raising the long-run debt-to-GDP ratio by an estimated 6.4 percentage points.
We documented that inflation expectations became de-anchored in 9 of 17 sampled economies following commodity price shocks exceeding two standard deviations above the historical mean.
We analyzed 23 OECD countries over four decades and found that independent central banks maintained average inflation rates 2.3 percentage points lower than those under direct government control.

We decomposed aggregate wage inequality into between-firm and within-firm components and found that between-firm dispersion accounted for approximately 68% of the total increase in earnings variance since 2000.
We estimated a marginal propensity to consume of 0.71 among households earning below $40,000 annually, substantially higher than the 0.43 coefficient observed among households earning above $120,000.

We examined wage growth trajectories across five income quintiles over a 20-year period and found that bottom-quintile workers experienced average annual real wage increases of just 0.3%, compared to 2.1% for top-quintile earners.

We constructed a dynamic scoring model incorporating behavioral responses and determined that proposed consumption tax reforms would generate net revenue gains of $340 billion over a ten-year window under baseline macroeconomic assumptions.

We constructed a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model and determined that optimal inflation targeting under supply uncertainty required a policy band of plus or minus 1.5 percentage points around the 2% benchmark.

We decomposed the sources of the United States–China bilateral trade deficit and found that factor endowment differentials and exchange rate misalignment together explained roughly 61% of the observed imbalance over our sample period.

We documented that unconventional monetary policy interventions, including quantitative easing programs totaling $4.5 trillion, suppressed the 10-year nominal yield by an estimated 120 basis points between 2009 and 2014.

We examined housing price dynamics across 142 metropolitan areas over a 20-year period, finding that a one-percentage-point increase in mortgage rates corresponded to an average 6.3% decline in home sales volume.

We decomposed household expenditure data from the Consumer Expenditure Survey into 14 spending categories and found that food-at-home spending remained the most income-inelastic category, with an elasticity coefficient of 0.31.

We examined the transmission of monetary policy shocks across 47 commercial banks and found that a 100 basis point increase in the federal funds rate reduced loan origination volumes by an average of 8.3% over a six-month horizon.
We estimated that a 10 percent depreciation of the domestic currency was associated with a 6.2 percent increase in export volumes within three quarters of the shock.
We investigated the pass-through effects of import price inflation on domestic consumer prices and observed a 0.47 elasticity coefficient in economies with flexible exchange rate regimes.

We tracked daily trading volumes and return correlations across six asset classes during the 2020 global financial disruption and observed that safe-haven flows into government securities increased by 340% relative to the prior 90-day baseline.

We constructed a panel dataset spanning 22 years of household income records and identified that wage stagnation in the bottom two quintiles suppressed aggregate consumer spending growth by an estimated 1.8 percentage points annually.

We identified a nonlinear relationship between GDP per capita growth and wage share of national income, observing that growth rates exceeding 5% annually were associated with declining labor share by an average of 1.9 percentage points.
We investigated the pass-through of nominal exchange rate movements to domestic import prices and estimated an average pass-through coefficient of 0.42 across 30 OECD economies over a 15-year window.

We estimated a search-and-matching model using Current Population Survey microdata and found that matching efficiency declined by 22% between 2007 and 2011, accounting for a substantial share of the observed unemployment persistence.

We observed that inflation persistence, measured by the sum of autoregressive coefficients, declined from 0.87 to 0.61 following the adoption of explicit inflation targeting frameworks across 24 emerging market economies.

We investigated whether bank capital adequacy ratios predicted subsequent credit contraction events across a panel of 23 OECD economies over a 15-year window, identifying a statistically significant threshold effect at the 8.2 percent tier-one capital ratio.

We documented that countries participating in regional trade agreements with explicit currency stabilization clauses experienced 22% lower bilateral exchange rate volatility and a corresponding 9.7% increase in intra-bloc trade volumes relative to non-member economies over the same interval.
We employed a structural vector autoregression framework and found that a positive fiscal shock equivalent to 1 percent of GDP raised private consumption by 0.31 percent over a two-year horizon.

We analyzed longitudinal survey data from 12,400 low-income households and found that access to formal credit markets reduced the probability of falling below the poverty line by 14.6 percentage points over a five-year horizon.
We investigated the pass-through effects of federal funds rate changes on 30-year fixed mortgage rates and found a long-run elasticity of 0.87 across our sample of 1,200 lending institutions.

We tested the repo market collateral haircut sensitivity to sovereign credit rating downgrades using transaction-level data from 2010 to 2020 and recorded an average haircut increase of 6.8 percentage points following a two-notch rating revision.

We constructed a repeat-sales price index for 48 major urban markets and found that real housing returns averaged 1.2 percent annually after controlling for inflation, substantially below the 4.1 percent nominal figure commonly cited in policy discussions.
We examined the pass-through effects of exchange rate fluctuations on domestic import prices across 24 OECD economies over a 15-year period, finding an average pass-through coefficient of 0.43.

We decomposed bank net interest margins across four recessionary periods and found that margins contracted by an average of 22 basis points during inverted yield curve episodes lasting more than six months.

We investigated whether the J-curve effect was present in the trade balances of seven Southeast Asian economies following the 2013 taper tantrum, observing a statistically significant short-run deterioration of approximately 3.1% in the current account before a gradual recovery emerged after 18 months.
We demonstrated that fiscal consolidation episodes characterized by spending cuts of at least 3% of GDP were associated with a mean output contraction of 2.4% over the subsequent two years.
We showed that targeted government transfers to households earning below $30,000 annually produced a consumption multiplier of 2.1, substantially exceeding that of upper-income transfers.

We investigated wage growth disparities across the bottom two income quintiles and observed that real hourly earnings stagnated at an average annual rate of 0.4% over the three decades following trade liberalization.

We applied a difference-in-differences framework to quarterly CPS data and observed that trade liberalization episodes between 1990 and 2005 accounted for roughly 22 percent of the observed increase in long-term unemployment.

We tested whether high-frequency trading activity amplified intraday price volatility using millisecond-level order book data from four major exchanges, finding a positive and significant relationship at the 1% significance level.

We investigated the relationship between minimum wage increases and youth unemployment in 48 U.S. states between 1990 and 2015, finding that a 10 percent rise in the minimum wage was associated with a 1.8 percent reduction in teenage employment.

We demonstrated that anchored inflation expectations, proxied by five-year forward breakeven rates, attenuated the pass-through of commodity price shocks to consumer prices by approximately 35 percent.
We estimated the elasticity of corporate bond spreads with respect to changes in the overnight repo rate and found a statistically significant coefficient of 0.74 across investment-grade instruments.

We analyzed the spatial spillover effects of foreclosed properties and documented that each additional foreclosure within a 0.1-mile radius reduced neighboring home values by an average of 1.1 percent during the 2007–2009 contraction.

We constructed a panel dataset of 12,000 household credit accounts spanning 2005 to 2019 and observed that subprime borrowers experienced disproportionately larger credit limit reductions during periods of elevated interbank lending rates.
We quantified the deadweight loss associated with marginal effective tax rates above 55%, estimating efficiency costs of approximately $18.6 billion annually for the sampled economies.

We evaluated the long-run distributional consequences of a revenue-neutral shift from income taxation to consumption taxation and found that the bottom two income deciles experienced welfare losses averaging 4.7 percent of annual consumption.

We employed a difference-in-differences framework to show that banks subject to Basel III capital requirements reduced their corporate loan portfolios by 9.3 percent relative to unaffected institutions between 2013 and 2017.

We estimated the sacrifice ratio for 31 advanced economies and found that disinflation programs implemented during periods of low unemployment required, on average, a 2.1 percent cumulative GDP loss per percentage point reduction in inflation.
We investigated the pass-through rate of central bank policy adjustments to retail deposit interest rates across 18 OECD economies and found an average long-run pass-through coefficient of 0.61.

We employed a structural VAR framework to identify exogenous fiscal policy shocks and estimated that a one percentage point increase in the tax burden reduced GDP growth by 0.31 percentage points over a two-year horizon.

We found that fiscal redistribution reduced market income inequality by an average of 8.4 Gini points in advanced economies, with the largest effects observed in Scandinavian countries where transfers accounted for 6.1 points of that reduction.
We examined unemployment duration across 14 OECD countries from 1995 to 2018, finding that a one percentage point increase in the replacement rate extended average jobless spells by 2.3 weeks.

We estimated that a one-standard-deviation increase in the VIX corresponded to a 180 basis point widening in corporate credit spreads, controlling for macroeconomic fundamentals and firm-level leverage ratios.

We compared rule-based and discretionary monetary policy frameworks across 52 countries and found that economies adhering to explicit inflation targeting maintained average annual inflation rates 2.8 percentage points lower over the 2000 to 2015 period.
We estimated that non-performing loan ratios increased by 1.8 percentage points for every 50 basis point rise in benchmark interest rates among mid-sized regional banks in our sample.

We measured the dispersion of small business loan approval rates across regional banks segmented by asset size and found that institutions holding fewer than 5 billion dollars in assets rejected applications at a rate 19 percentage points higher than larger counterparts.

We tested the validity of purchasing power parity for a panel of 40 developing economies over a 30-year horizon, and our panel cointegration results supported long-run PPP convergence in 31 of the 40 cases at the 5% significance level.

We constructed a conditional value-at-risk framework and observed that tail risk exposures in emerging market portfolios exceeded those of developed market benchmarks by a factor of 2.3 during currency crises.
We documented that workers transitioning from routine-task occupations faced median earnings reductions of $6,400 annually and required an average of 14 months to secure stable reemployment.

We measured the responsiveness of housing starts to changes in real interest rates across 18 OECD economies and found a mean elasticity of negative 0.64, with considerable heterogeneity among countries with differing mortgage market structures.

We measured the responsiveness of consumer credit card interest rates to federal funds rate changes and found an asymmetric adjustment pattern in which rates rose 1.4 times faster than they fell following equivalent policy shifts.
We observed that subnational governments facing hard budget constraints reduced per-pupil education expenditures by an average of $340 annually following the removal of federal bailout provisions.

We analyzed 22 years of retail sales data and observed that consumer spending on non-essential goods contracted by an average of 4.1% in the six months following a 0.5 percentage point rise in the unemployment rate.

We analyzed zoning deregulation episodes across 67 municipalities and found that upzoning policies reducing minimum lot size requirements by 50 percent generated a 9.4 percent increase in housing supply over five years.
We documented that shadow banking sector assets grew by 340 percent between 2002 and 2016, accounting for nearly 28 percent of total financial intermediation in our sample of G20 economies.

We tested whether progressive marginal tax rate increases above 65 percent generated measurable distortions in reported labor income, finding a compensated elasticity of taxable income of 0.31 among high-earning professionals.

We examined 47 episodes of fiscal consolidation across emerging market economies and observed that expenditure-based adjustments reduced sovereign borrowing spreads by an average of 112 basis points within 18 months.

We analyzed the heterogeneous effects of austerity measures on GDP per capita and found that expenditure-based consolidations reduced growth by 1.7 percentage points more than revenue-based consolidations of equivalent magnitude.
We analyzed credit default swap spreads for 312 financial institutions and observed that systemic risk premia widened by an average of 84 basis points during the 2008 liquidity crisis.
We analyzed the spillover effects of foreclosure clustering and found that each additional foreclosure within a 250-meter radius depressed surrounding property values by an average of 4.1 percent.

We estimated the labour force participation elasticity among prime-age workers aged 25 to 54 and found that a one percentage point increase in local wage growth corresponded to a 0.34 percentage point rise in participation rates.

We found that trade policy uncertainty, as measured by our constructed index, reduced cross-border investment commitments by 17 percent during episodes of heightened tariff dispute activity between 2016 and 2020.
We documented that the dollar invoicing share in global trade exceeded 79% in our sample, amplifying the spillover effects of US monetary policy shocks on third-country trade volumes.

We modeled the transmission of housing price volatility to broader financial stability indicators across 18 OECD countries and observed that a 10 percent decline in residential property values corresponded to a 0.31-percentage-point increase in nonperforming loan ratios within three quarters.
We measured the sacrifice ratio at 1.9 percentage points of GDP per one percentage point reduction in inflation during contractionary monetary episodes between 1980 and 2019.

We identified a nonlinear relationship between money supply growth and consumer price inflation, with effects becoming statistically significant only above a threshold of 6% annual monetary expansion.
We found that central bank forward guidance reduced long-term inflation expectations by 0.6 percentage points in economies with high institutional credibility scores.

We constructed a repeat-sales price index for 1.4 million single-family transactions and observed that post-2020 remote work adoption accelerated suburban price growth at roughly 2.3 times the rate of urban core appreciation.

We constructed a dynamic scoring model and determined that proposed capital gains tax reductions would generate a net revenue loss of approximately $47 billion over a ten-year budget window under realistic behavioral response assumptions.
We found that exchange rate volatility accounted for approximately 23 percent of the observed decline in export volumes among small open economies during the 2008 financial crisis.

We constructed a panel dataset covering 23 OECD economies from 1995 to 2019 and found that a 100 basis point increase in the policy rate reduced household credit growth by approximately 3.2 percentage points.

We analyzed 47 episodes of hyperinflation between 1920 and 2010 and found that fiscal deficits exceeding 12 percent of GDP preceded monetary collapse in 89 percent of cases by an average of 14 months.

We quantified the spillover of sovereign bond yield volatility from peripheral eurozone economies to core markets and estimated that each 100 basis point shock to Italian yields transmitted a 37 basis point secondary effect to German bunds.

We identified a statistically significant negative relationship between value-added tax rates and small business formation, with each five-point rate increase associated with an 11 percent reduction in new firm registrations.
We measured the welfare costs of non-tariff barriers in agricultural trade among ASEAN member states and estimated aggregate efficiency losses equivalent to 2.1% of regional GDP annually.

We identified three distinct volatility regimes using a Markov-switching GARCH framework applied to S&P 500 intraday data spanning 2005 to 2022, with high-volatility states persisting for an average of 14.7 trading days.
We identified significant asymmetries in exchange rate pass-through, observing that currency depreciations transmitted to consumer prices at nearly twice the rate of equivalent appreciations.

We analyzed the trade balance responses of 19 eurozone member states following the introduction of the common currency and documented a persistent current account divergence averaging 3.4% of GDP among peripheral economies.
We analyzed consumption responses to the 2008 tax rebate program and observed that lower-income households spent approximately 70 percent of their rebate within three months of receipt.

We constructed a poverty transition matrix from five waves of panel survey data and determined that 41% of households experiencing transient poverty episodes failed to achieve sustained income stability within a 10-year horizon.

We estimated a dynamic factor model using daily returns from 312 financial institutions and identified three latent systemic risk components that collectively explained 71% of sector-wide volatility clustering.

We documented that unconventional monetary policy interventions, specifically quantitative easing programs totaling $4.5 trillion, compressed 10-year Treasury yields by an average of 120 basis points between 2009 and 2014.

We identified a structural break in the Beveridge curve in 2009, indicating that matching efficiency in U.S. labor markets deteriorated by an estimated 22 percent in the aftermath of the financial crisis.

We examined household income elasticity across 14,320 surveyed families and found that a 10% increase in disposable income corresponded to a 6.3% rise in discretionary consumer spending over the observed three-year period.

We estimated the elasticity of skilled-to-unskilled wage ratios with respect to trade openness at 0.31, suggesting that import competition contributed meaningfully to observed within-country wage divergence.

We documented that intergenerational income mobility declined by approximately 12% across cohorts born between 1960 and 1984 in the United States, as measured by rank-rank correlations in parent–child earnings.
We analyzed consumption inequality using expenditure microdata from 28 countries and found that the top decile's consumption share exceeded 30% in 19 of those economies during our study period.

We investigated the cyclical component of long-term unemployment using quarterly data from 1980 to 2022 and found that structural unemployment accounted for roughly 43 percent of the post-recession jobless rate.

We identified a nonlinear relationship between public education expenditure and long-run productivity growth, estimating that spending increases beyond 6.5% of GDP yielded diminishing marginal returns of approximately 0.11% per additional percentage point.

We applied a GARCH-DCC framework to daily closing prices of 12 major currency pairs and observed that cross-asset correlations spiked by an average of 0.41 standard deviations in the 30-day window following Federal Reserve rate announcements.

We examined housing price appreciation across 312 metropolitan statistical areas between 2000 and 2020, finding that a one percentage point increase in local employment growth corresponded to a 2.3 percent rise in median home values.

We documented that households experiencing unemployment spells lasting longer than six months reduced total consumption expenditure by an average of 22.7%, with the sharpest declines concentrated in durable goods categories.

We investigated the predictive power of credit default swap spreads for corporate bond market liquidity disruptions across a sample of 1,240 investment-grade firms, finding that a 50-basis-point widening in CDS spreads preceded illiquidity episodes by approximately 18 trading days.

We employed a network-based contagion model calibrated to interbank exposure data from 18 economies and estimated that the failure of the three most interconnected nodes would trigger cascading losses equivalent to 6.2% of aggregate system assets.
We investigated bilateral trade flows between 67 country pairs and found that exchange rate volatility reduced trade volumes by approximately 8.4 percent on average.

We applied an instrumental variables approach to isolate the causal effect of tax rebate transfers on spending behavior and found that households with incomes below $35,000 spent 74% of their rebates within 90 days of receipt.
We estimated that a 100 basis point surprise tightening by the Federal Reserve produced a 1.2% depreciation in emerging market currencies within a 48-hour trading window.

We applied a spatial autoregressive model to county-level housing data and observed that infrastructure investment in public transit corridors increased proximate residential property values by an average of 8.3 percent within a half-mile radius.
We quantified the fiscal multiplier associated with defense procurement spending and estimated a value of 0.74 during periods of economic expansion, falling to 0.31 during contractionary phases.

We found that exchange rate depreciation of 10 percent transmitted into domestic producer price inflation at a rate of approximately 4.1 percent within two quarters, with significantly stronger pass-through observed in economies with dollarized debt structures.

We identified a nonlinear relationship between money supply growth and inflation expectations, with effects becoming statistically significant only when M2 growth exceeded 8.5 percent annually in our sample of 29 developing economies.

We analyzed consumption smoothing behavior across 6,200 households following unexpected job loss events and observed a sharp 29% contraction in non-essential spending within the first two quarters of income disruption.

We examined the portfolio losses of 312 institutional investors during the 2020 market dislocation and found that funds with greater illiquidity exposure suffered median drawdowns 11.2 percentage points deeper than their more liquid counterparts.

We investigated the nonlinear effects of public debt on GDP growth and determined that economies exceeding a debt-to-GDP ratio of 90 percent experienced growth rates approximately 1.7 percentage points lower than their less-indebted counterparts.

We measured the impact of credit rating downgrades on corporate bond yields and observed an average immediate yield increase of 87 basis points following a one-notch downgrade by major rating agencies.

We decomposed regional house price growth into demand-side and supply-side components and found that income growth explained approximately 41 percent of price appreciation in supply-constrained metropolitan areas.

We employed a regression discontinuity design around the 50-employee firm-size threshold and found that payroll tax mandates reduced net hiring by 6.4 percent among firms near the regulatory boundary.

We measured the elasticity of labor supply among low-income households at 0.43, suggesting that marginal increases in earned income tax credits produced meaningful but bounded increases in workforce participation.
We measured the pass-through rate from aggregate income gains to retail consumer spending at 0.64 during expansion phases, compared to a markedly lower rate of 0.31 during contractionary periods.
We estimated that fiscal stimulus packages averaging 2.3% of GDP reduced output gaps by approximately 1.8 percentage points across 24 OECD economies during the post-recession recovery period.

We estimated that a one percentage point increase in government expenditure as a share of GDP led to a 0.43 percentage point rise in output growth across 47 emerging market economies over the 2000–2019 period.

We estimated counterfactual income distributions under alternative tax and transfer regimes and concluded that a 5-percentage-point increase in the top marginal tax rate would reduce the 90-10 earnings ratio by approximately 0.14 units.

We measured the impact of Basel III capital adequacy requirements on credit supply and documented a 3.2 percentage point reduction in annual lending growth among undercapitalized institutions between 2011 and 2015.

We constructed a systemic risk index drawing on balance sheet data from 230 financial institutions across G20 economies and found that leverage ratios above 18:1 were associated with a 62% higher probability of contagion spillover.

We analyzed the heterogeneous effects of the 2018–2019 US–China tariff escalation on third-country export diversion and found that Vietnam, Mexico, and Taiwan collectively captured an additional $28.4 billion in US import market share during the two-year period.

We examined the impact of credit default swap spreads on corporate bond liquidity across 1,200 investment-grade firms and found that a 100 basis point widening in CDS spreads corresponded to a 17% reduction in secondary market trading volume.

We used difference-in-differences estimation to evaluate stimulus payment effects on retail spending and observed a statistically significant 11.4% increase in consumer transactions among households earning under $50,000 annually.

We decomposed GDP growth into its expenditure components and found that government consumption contributed a statistically significant 0.8 percentage points to annual output expansion in high-debt economies.

We estimated a threshold regression model and found that public debt levels exceeding 87 percent of GDP were associated with a statistically significant 1.2 percentage point reduction in average annual growth rates among advanced economies.

We applied a panel vector autoregression framework to data from 22 developing economies and found that tax revenue shocks of 2 percent of GDP generated persistent contractions in private investment lasting an average of six quarters.

We evaluated the effectiveness of central bank forward guidance in reducing long-term interest rate uncertainty and found that explicit policy commitments reduced 10-year yield forecast dispersion by approximately 22 basis points across 12 advanced economies.

We quantified tail-risk dependence between housing price indices and bank equity valuations in 19 advanced economies and found that lower-tail co-movement intensified by a factor of 2.3 during periods when household debt-to-GDP ratios exceeded 85%.

We documented that youth unemployment rates in the eurozone periphery exceeded 45% during the sovereign debt crisis period, with scarring effects persisting for at least seven subsequent years in our longitudinal sample.

We constructed a panel dataset covering 230,000 displaced workers across five European economies and found that re-employment probabilities declined by 12 percent for each additional six months spent outside the labor force.
We estimated the income elasticity of housing demand at 1.14 for first-time buyers and 0.89 for repeat buyers, using a dataset of 2.3 million mortgage originations between 2010 and 2022.

We estimated that a 1% increase in trade openness was associated with a 0.18% widening of the 90/10 wage percentile ratio in emerging market economies, controlling for institutional quality and human capital endowments.
We estimated a labor demand elasticity of -0.43 with respect to payroll taxes using firm-level administrative records covering over 800,000 establishments across eight European economies.

We analyzed current account adjustment dynamics across 55 countries and determined that a 1 percent improvement in the terms of trade reduced the current account deficit by approximately 0.6 percentage points within four quarters.

We analyzed household income data from 12,847 survey respondents across five income quintiles and found that a 10% increase in disposable income corresponded to a 6.3% rise in discretionary consumer spending over the observed 24-month period.

We measured daily return volatility across 47 emerging market equity indices over a 15-year period and found that cross-market contagion amplified drawdowns by an average of 23.4 percentage points during systemic stress episodes.

We measured the elasticity of skilled versus unskilled wages with respect to technological adoption and estimated that automation-exposed workers faced cumulative real wage losses of 8.3% over a decade.

We measured the elasticity of labor supply among workers in the bottom two income deciles and found a value of 0.61, suggesting substantial responsiveness to marginal wage increases in this population.

We analyzed the relationship between policy uncertainty indices and stock market volatility in G7 economies and found that a one-standard-deviation increase in uncertainty corresponded to a 6.4 percentage point rise in annualized return volatility.

We tested whether targeted cash transfer programs of $75 per month reduced extreme poverty rates and found statistically significant decreases of 14.2 percentage points among beneficiary households in our longitudinal panel.

We estimated that a 1 percentage point increase in government expenditure as a share of GDP was associated with a 0.43 percentage point rise in output growth over the 1990–2015 period across 42 OECD economies.
We found that a 10-percentage-point increase in union membership density was associated with a 6.3% reduction in the Gini coefficient across 42 OECD economies between 1990 and 2018.

We applied a threshold vector autoregression framework to quarterly credit spread data spanning four decades and identified nonlinear adjustment dynamics in which spreads above 450 basis points triggered self-reinforcing contractionary credit cycles.

We tested whether permanent income shocks produced larger consumption responses than transitory shocks, finding that permanent shocks generated expenditure adjustments roughly 2.4 times greater in magnitude across our panel of 6,200 households.

We decomposed the yield curve term premium into cyclical and structural components across seven advanced economies and found that the structural component explained approximately 63 percent of observed long-run variation in 10-year sovereign bond yields.

We estimated that households in the bottom two income quintiles allocated approximately 78% of marginal income gains to essential goods and services, compared to only 34% among households in the top quintile.

We applied a panel vector autoregression framework to quarterly data from 34 countries and found that positive fiscal shocks equivalent to 1 percent of GDP generated peak output responses of 0.9 percent within six quarters.

We investigated the transmission of financial contagion across sovereign debt markets during the 2010–2012 European crisis and found that cross-border spillover effects amplified yield spreads by an average of 187 basis points.

We decomposed the gender wage gap using matched employer-employee data from 3.2 million observations and found that occupational sorting explained 31 percent of the remaining 14.7 percent earnings differential.
We documented that tax revenue shortfalls exceeding 3 percent of GDP were followed by sovereign credit rating downgrades in 67 percent of the 94 episodes we examined.

We tested whether automatic stabilizers accounted for a measurable share of output variance and confirmed that they explained approximately 28 percent of the reduction in GDP volatility observed across OECD economies between 1985 and 2018.

We constructed a consumption smoothing model using data from 47 metropolitan areas and found that households with fewer than three months of liquid savings reduced spending by 14.2% more severely during income shocks than their more financially resilient counterparts.

We analyzed consumer spending panel data from 4,200 households and observed that unexpected income windfalls of $1,000 or more generated a marginal propensity to consume of 0.62 within the same fiscal quarter.

We measured the conditional volatility of equity returns across 23 emerging markets over a 15-year horizon, finding that cross-border capital flow reversals amplified price swings by an average of 34 percent relative to baseline periods.
We examined quarterly credit spreads across 847 U.S. financial institutions from 1995 to 2019 and observed a mean widening of 43 basis points during periods of monetary tightening.

We constructed a panel dataset spanning 38 emerging market economies and observed that fiscal multipliers were substantially larger during periods of economic slack, averaging 1.6 compared to 0.7 during expansions.

We applied a dynamic conditional correlation model to 30 years of commodity futures data and found that gold served as an effective volatility hedge in 78% of equity market downturns exceeding a 15% peak-to-trough decline.
We examined the pass-through rate of central bank policy rates to retail lending rates across 47 commercial banks, finding an average transmission elasticity of 0.73 over a 12-month horizon.

We documented that household debt service ratios exceeded 18 percent of disposable income in seven of the ten metropolitan areas we examined, a level historically associated with elevated rates of consumer loan delinquency.

We assessed the heterogeneous impact of fiscal multipliers across business cycle phases and observed that government spending multipliers were 0.6 units larger during recessionary periods than during expansions.

We employed a regression discontinuity design around the Basel III capital threshold and observed that banks required to hold an additional 2 percentage points of Tier 1 capital reduced their corporate lending portfolios by 6.3 percent on average.

We investigated the marginal propensity to consume among low-income households earning below $35,000 annually and determined that each additional dollar of transfer income generated $0.89 in new consumption within the same fiscal quarter.

We constructed a panel dataset spanning 32 OECD economies from 1995 to 2019 and found that a 10 percent increase in minimum wage levels was associated with a 1.4 percent reduction in youth employment rates.

We evaluated the wage scarring effects of early-career unemployment and found that workers who experienced joblessness exceeding 12 months before age 30 earned on average 14 percent less per year over the subsequent decade compared to continuously employed peers.
We estimated that zoning restriction indices explained approximately 34 percent of the cross-sectional variation in housing affordability ratios observed between 2005 and 2020.

We found that automation exposure, measured as the share of routine task intensity in local employment, explained 31 percent of the cross-regional variance in long-term unemployment rates observed between 2000 and 2018.

We estimated value-at-risk thresholds for a diversified portfolio of sovereign bonds using Monte Carlo simulation with 100,000 iterations and found that the 99th percentile loss exceeded conventional Basel III capital buffer requirements by a margin of 8.3 percentage points.

We examined housing price appreciation across 42 metropolitan areas over a 15-year period and found that proximity to high-frequency transit corridors increased residential property values by an average of 18.3 percent.

We estimated the welfare gains from trade liberalization using a quantitative general equilibrium model and found that eliminating remaining tariff barriers would raise real income by 2.1% in low-income countries.

We applied a regression discontinuity design to municipal budget data and found that jurisdictions crossing the debt ceiling threshold reduced public employment by an average of 6.2 percent.

We tracked homeownership rates across income quintiles from 1990 to 2022 and found that the gap between the top and bottom quintile widened by 19 percentage points, driven largely by down payment affordability constraints.

We tracked consumption responses following a $1,200 federal stimulus disbursement and observed that lower-income households spent 89% of the transfer within 30 days, while higher-income households spent only 52%.
We applied a gravity model framework to 28 years of bilateral trade data and found that a 1% reduction in tariff rates corresponded to a 1.6% increase in trade volumes between partnered economies.

We constructed a panel dataset covering 62 countries from 1980 to 2020 and found that infrastructure investment multipliers exceeded 1.5 when the output gap was negative and monetary policy rates were at the zero lower bound.

We measured the vacancy-to-unemployment ratio across 78 metropolitan statistical areas and demonstrated that matching efficiency declined by approximately 17 percent during the 2008 financial crisis, with recovery lagging significantly in regions with high occupational concentration.
We documented that the college wage premium widened from 48% to 74% between 1985 and 2015, with the steepest increases concentrated among workers in the highest-skill cognitive task occupations.

We estimated that eliminating the mortgage interest deduction would reduce average housing prices by 3.8 percent in high-cost metropolitan areas while increasing federal revenue by approximately $72 billion annually.

We investigated the role of currency misalignment in shaping current account balances across 28 emerging market economies and found that a 1% overvaluation was associated with a 0.4 percentage point deterioration in the trade balance.
We constructed a time-varying parameter model spanning 1975 to 2022 and identified three distinct monetary policy regimes characterized by significantly different inflation persistence parameters.

We found that targeted fiscal transfers to households in the bottom income quintile generated a multiplier effect of approximately 1.8, significantly exceeding the 0.9 multiplier observed for upper-quintile recipients.

We analyzed 43 years of monthly CPI data and identified that energy price shocks accounted for roughly 31 percent of total inflation variance in commodity-importing advanced economies.

We constructed a firm-level panel of over 4,800 publicly listed companies and observed that leverage ratios above 60% were associated with a 41% amplification in idiosyncratic return volatility during credit tightening cycles.

We examined housing price dynamics across 42 metropolitan areas over a 15-year period and found that a one percentage point increase in mortgage rates was associated with a 6.3 percent decline in home sales volume.
We decomposed earnings inequality using Theil index components and determined that between-sector wage divergence accounted for approximately 62% of total income inequality growth from 1990 to 2018.

We examined unemployment dynamics across 28 OECD countries over a 15-year period and found that a one percentage point increase in interest rates corresponded to a 0.4 percentage point rise in the short-term unemployment rate.

We examined the relationship between discretionary fiscal spending and GDP growth across 47 OECD economies over a 30-year period, finding that a one percentage point increase in public investment yielded an average output multiplier of 1.6.

We tested whether quantitative easing programs reduced inflation volatility and found statistically significant reductions in conditional variance of approximately 22 percent across our panel of G7 economies.

We constructed a repeat-sales price index for single-family residential properties and documented an average annual real appreciation rate of 2.1 percent in supply-constrained coastal markets.

We tracked consumer spending patterns over a 15-year panel dataset and observed a statistically significant 2.3 percentage point decline in durable goods purchases following each 100 basis point increase in interest rates.

We tested the Fisher hypothesis across 38 emerging market economies and observed that only 14 exhibited a statistically significant long-run one-to-one relationship between nominal interest rates and expected inflation at the 5 percent significance level.

We identified a persistent 18% gap in per capita consumer spending between rural and urban households after controlling for regional price differences, income levels, and household size across our nationally representative sample.

We assessed the relationship between yield curve inversions and subsequent recessionary periods and found that inversions exceeding 30 basis points predicted economic contractions with 74 percent accuracy over our 60-year sample.

We constructed a systemic risk index for 48 globally systemically important financial institutions from 2005 to 2022, and we found that leverage ratios above 18:1 predicted distress propagation with a precision rate of 81 percent.

We analysed sectoral reallocation following the 2008 financial crisis and found that workers transitioning from construction to services experienced median earnings losses of approximately 18,700 dollars over three years.

We investigated the relationship between housing wealth appreciation and consumer spending in 38 U.S. metropolitan markets and documented that a $10,000 increase in home equity corresponded to approximately $620 in additional annual household expenditure.

We estimated marginal propensities to consume across five income brackets using longitudinal survey data from 2001 to 2019 and found the lowest quintile exhibited an MPC of 0.91 compared to 0.43 for the highest quintile.

We constructed a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model calibrated to eurozone data and found that a 10 percent increase in infrastructure spending raised steady-state GDP by 3.4 percent over a five-year horizon.

We employed a threshold error-correction model to assess asymmetric exchange rate pass-through in Brazil and found that depreciation episodes transmitted to consumer prices at a rate of 0.38, while appreciation episodes yielded a significantly weaker pass-through coefficient of 0.19.
We investigated the pass-through effects of monetary tightening on consumer price indices across 18 OECD economies and observed that the median adjustment lag was approximately 6.3 quarters.

We estimated that each additional year of central bank governor tenure was associated with a 0.12 percentage point reduction in mean annual inflation, holding monetary regime and fiscal balance constant.
We measured the long-run elasticity of GDP with respect to infrastructure spending at 0.15, drawing on data from 55 low- and middle-income countries over a 30-year window.

We estimated tail risk exposures using a conditional value-at-risk approach and observed that the 99th percentile loss threshold for leveraged institutional portfolios exceeded conventional VaR estimates by a factor of 2.3.

We tested whether geopolitical risk indices, constructed from 2.4 million news articles, had incremental predictive power over standard financial variables for forecasting realized volatility in oil futures, and confirmed a statistically significant relationship at the 1% level.
We examined the impact of a 10 percent yuan depreciation on bilateral trade flows between China and its 47 major trading partners over the period 2005–2019.

We estimated that a 10% increase in the minimum wage was associated with a 6.2% reduction in the poverty headcount ratio among households with at least one full-time low-wage worker.

We examined intraday bid-ask spreads across three major stock exchanges from 2005 to 2022 and documented that market liquidity deteriorated by roughly 27% during episodes of geopolitical uncertainty lasting longer than two weeks.

We examined bilateral trade flows between 42 country pairs over a 30-year period and found that a 10% depreciation in the real effective exchange rate corresponded to a 6.3% increase in export volumes on average.

We analyzed fiscal consolidation episodes in 22 emerging market economies and observed that expenditure-based adjustments produced smaller GDP losses than tax-based adjustments by a margin of 1.1 percentage points on average.

We tested whether extended unemployment insurance benefits beyond 26 weeks reduced re-employment rates and found a statistically significant 0.8 percentage point decline in monthly job-finding probability for each additional week of eligibility.

We measured the capitalization of school quality into residential property values and estimated a price premium of approximately 8,700 dollars per standard deviation improvement in district-level test scores.

We investigated the wealth effects of house price appreciation on household consumption and estimated a marginal propensity to consume out of housing wealth of 0.032 among homeowners aged 55 and older.
We investigated the pass-through of import price inflation to domestic consumer prices and observed a coefficient of 0.31, substantially lower than estimates from pre-2008 literature.

We investigated the heterogeneous effects of value-added tax reforms across 29 countries and found that a 1 percentage point increase in the standard VAT rate reduced annual GDP growth by 0.19 percentage points on average.

We identified a statistically significant negative relationship between interbank lending rates and small business loan approval rates, with a one percentage point increase in LIBOR associated with a 6.1 percent reduction in approvals.

We tracked spending patterns across 3,200 middle-income households following the 2017 tax reform and documented an average annual increase of $1,340 in reported discretionary expenditures within the first fiscal year.

We investigated the causal relationship between minimum wage increases of $2.50 per hour and poverty reduction, finding a statistically significant 6.2 percentage point decline in household poverty rates within two years of implementation.

We analyzed fiscal multipliers across 47 countries and observed that government spending multipliers averaged 1.6 during recessionary periods, falling to 0.7 during expansionary phases of the business cycle.

We estimated that a one percentage point increase in the marginal corporate tax rate was associated with a 0.43 percent decline in domestic fixed investment across 28 OECD economies over the 2000–2018 period.

We estimated that a 10% reduction in median household income corresponded to a 6.8% contraction in discretionary consumer spending, with the largest effects concentrated in leisure and hospitality sectors.

We decomposed realized variance for the S&P 500 into continuous and jump components across four recessionary periods, observing that discontinuous price movements accounted for 41 percent of total return variance during peak stress months.

We employed a regression discontinuity design to assess the spending response to the 2021 stimulus transfers and estimated that households in the $40,000–$75,000 income bracket increased monthly expenditures by an average of $312 within 30 days of receipt.

We tracked spending patterns across 18 product categories and found that durable goods purchases declined by 14.3% among middle-income households during periods of elevated inflation exceeding 5% annually.

We constructed a quarterly panel of 180 regional labour markets and found that fiscal stimulus packages reduced peak unemployment rates by approximately 1.8 percentage points relative to untreated regions.

We measured intergenerational income elasticity at 0.52 in low-mobility regions versus 0.31 in high-mobility regions, suggesting that geographic sorting amplifies inequality transmission across generations.
